extracted.intended_audience: public relations students, PR practitioners, and communications writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for public relations writing broadly, with chapters addressing press releases, media writing, message design, ethics/legal responsibilities, research, and formats across print, broadcast, and digital channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and legal responsibility of the PR writer
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical and legal responsibility of the PR writer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The edition represents the ethical and legal responsibilities of PR writing; implies adherence to laws, truthfulness, and professional ethics when producing PR materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding persuasion techniques needed to write effectively; selecting appeals and strategies appropriate to publics and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research for the public relations writer
rubrics_metrics.description: Research for the public relations writer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the kinds of research a writer needs to do to inform messages and tactics (audience analysis, media research, background fact-checking).

rubrics_metrics.name: The public relations planning process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning steps that link objectives, audiences, strategies, tactics, and evaluation — ensuring press releases and other materials fit an overall PR plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing to clarify and simplify the complex: style and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing to clarify and simplify the complex: style and content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes clarity and simplification of complex information for publics; stylistic choices to make content accessible and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar, spelling and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental mechanical correctness required for professional PR writing; adherence to standard usage to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for select publics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailoring tone, format, and content to specific audiences (internal vs. external publics, stakeholders, media, consumers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Email, memos, letters, reports and proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Email, memos, letters, reports and proposals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and formats for internal and targeted external communications — appropriate structure, concision, and purpose-driven content for each form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for mass media publics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles for writing materials intended for mass media distribution, including newsworthiness, media conventions, and pitching considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: News releases for print media
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidance on preparing press/news releases for newspapers and print outlets — likely includes headline, lede, nut graph, inverted pyramid, boilerplate, and contact info.

rubrics_metrics.name: News for broadcasting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptation of news release content and style for broadcast media (audio/visual constraints, shorter copy, writing for the ear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Features for print and broadcasting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on writing feature stories across media: narrative techniques, human interest focus, structure differences from hard news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message design concepts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concepts for crafting strategic messages (message mapping, framing, key points) to ensure consistency and persuasion across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing advertising copy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles and techniques for short-form persuasive copy used in adverts and paid placements; emphasis on call-to-action and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for the internet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices for online content: scannability, SEO-aware headings, multimedia integration, concise web-friendly sentence/paragraph structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media kits and media pitches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for assembling press kits and pitching journalists: what materials to include, packaging, timing, and personalization of pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speeches and other presentations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on speechwriting and presentation materials: structure, rhetoric, audience adaptation, and delivery-conscious writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for newsletter content, frequency, audience segmentation, and balance of news vs. promotional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brochures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for brochure copy: concise messaging, visual-text balance, reader orientation, and calls-to-action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazines and annual reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer-form organizational publications standards: feature writing, tone for stakeholders, factual accuracy, and design-copy integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles for communicating during crises: timeliness, transparency, holding statements, message consistency, and legal/ethical caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability formulas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of readability measures (e.g., Flesch) to assess and adjust text complexity for target audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyfitting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques to fit copy into fixed space constraints (headlines, brochures, ads) while preserving clarity and key messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix C. Answers to AP style exercises
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to AP style conventions for consistency in punctuation, capitalization, and journalistic usage across press materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand how PR writing differs from literary writing
rubrics_metrics.description: It's very useful for you to understand what makes public relations writing different form literary writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes objective, audience-focused, persuasive, and clear communication rather than literary flourish; prioritize utility and accuracy.
